api.workflows.get.answers: which workflows are defined, with their entry steps and cron
api.workflows.get.never_for: whether a workflow is currently running — that is Redis L2

api.workflows.get_id.answers: one workflow's cron expression, entry steps and assignments by id
api.workflows.get_id.never_for: whether it is currently projected — L2 legitimately lags a PUT until the next start

api.workflows.post.answers: creates a workflow and its junction rows in one transaction: one WorkflowEntrySteps row per required entry-step id and one WorkflowAssignments row per assignment id
api.workflows.post.never_for: starting the workflow — creating the definition and projecting it into L2 are different actions; only orchestration/start does the latter

api.workflows.put_id.answers: updates a workflow's cron expression and replaces both junctions' rows for it — remove-and-replace, so the client submits the desired final entry-step and assignment sets
api.workflows.put_id.never_for: updating a running projection — L2 only re-syncs on the next start, so a PUT alone does not move it

api.workflows.delete_id.answers: deletes a workflow, cascading its own junction rows; blocked if a step or assignment it points at still exists, which raises SQLSTATE 23001 and a 422
api.workflows.delete_id.never_for: removing it from L2 — that is stop, not delete; deleting the definition while it is still projected leaves L2 pointing at a definition that no longer exists

api.orchestration.post_start.answers: accepting one workflow for projection, after five synchronous gates
api.orchestration.post_start.never_for: confirming the workflow is projected — 202 means accepted, not applied

api.orchestration.post_stop.answers: validates the workflow id and queues its removal from L2, returning 202
api.orchestration.post_stop.never_for: confirming L2 no longer holds the projection — 202 means the stop was queued and accepted, not applied

api.steps.get.answers: every step: its processor binding and entry condition
api.steps.get.never_for: the step's own successors — those live in the StepNextSteps junction, not on this row

api.steps.get_id.answers: one step's processor id and entry condition by id
api.steps.get_id.never_for: its outgoing edges — StepNextSteps, not this row

api.steps.post.answers: creates a step — a processor id (restrict FK) and an entry condition — and syncs its next-step set into StepNextSteps
api.steps.post.never_for: a ProcessorId naming nothing — that raises SQLSTATE 23503, surfaced through the exception mapper

api.steps.put_id.answers: updates a step's processor binding, entry condition, or next-step set
api.steps.put_id.never_for: a partial edit to the successor set — PUT replaces the whole StepNextSteps set for this step, it does not merge

api.steps.delete_id.answers: deletes a step; blocked while an assignment, a StepNextSteps edge, or a WorkflowEntrySteps row still references it
api.steps.delete_id.never_for: deleting a step still referenced elsewhere — restrict FK, surfaced as 422

api.schemas.get.answers: every schema: its JSON Schema draft 2020-12 document, stored as jsonb
api.schemas.get.never_for: whether a given definition is still editable — a schema referenced by any processor is frozen, and this listing does not say which

api.schemas.get_id.answers: one schema's Definition document by id
api.schemas.get_id.never_for: whether it is frozen — check for a referencing processor, or read the 409 a PUT would raise; this response does not carry that flag

api.schemas.post.answers: creates a schema; the document is parsed and validated against the draft 2020-12 meta-schema before it is persisted
api.schemas.post.never_for: accepting a document that merely parses as JSON — it must additionally validate as a JSON Schema

api.schemas.put_id.never_for: mutating a definition already referenced by a processor — that raises SchemaDefinitionFrozenException, surfaced as 409, and it never unfreezes

api.schemas.delete_id.answers: deletes a schema; blocked while any processor references it as input, output, or config
api.schemas.delete_id.never_for: deleting one a processor references — restrict FK, surfaced as 422

api.processors.get.answers: every registered processor: its SourceHash and its optional input/output/config schema ids
api.processors.get.never_for: whether a processor's replicas are alive right now — that is redis.PerInstance / redis.InstanceIndex

api.processors.get_id.never_for: its live replica count — that is redis.InstanceIndex

api.processors.post.answers: registers a processor: SourceHash plus optional schema ids; a duplicate hash is SQLSTATE 23505, surfaced as 409
api.processors.post.never_for: confirming the registration is reachable by a running deployment — a row existing and a processor binary being live are different facts

api.processors.put_id.answers: updates a processor's schema references or SourceHash
api.processors.put_id.never_for: confirming a changed SourceHash matches a rebuilt, redeployed binary — this only stores the value the API was told

api.processors.delete_id.answers: deletes a processor; blocked while a step still references it
api.processors.delete_id.never_for: deleting one a step references — SQLSTATE 23001, surfaced as 422

api.processors.get_by_source_hash_source.answers: the single processor row whose SourceHash matches the supplied route segment, by exact byte comparison
api.processors.get_by_source_hash_source.never_for: a mixed-case or uppercase hash — matching is case-sensitive against the lowercase 64-hex value the create validator enforces, so an uppercase variant 404s past a row that exists

api.assignments.get.answers: every assignment: a step id and its jsonb payload
api.assignments.get.never_for: which workflow includes it — only the WorkflowAssignments junction says that, not this row

api.assignments.get_id.answers: one assignment's step binding and payload by id
api.assignments.get_id.never_for: which workflow(s) include it — the WorkflowAssignments junction, not a column here

api.assignments.post.answers: creates an assignment: a step id plus a jsonb payload, validated for syntax and length only
api.assignments.post.never_for: payload validation against a schema — the assignment carries no schema reference, so none is possible at this layer

api.assignments.put_id.answers: updates an assignment's step binding or payload
api.assignments.put_id.never_for: changing which workflow includes it — that is WorkflowAssignments, synced only through the workflow's own PUT

api.assignments.delete_id.answers: deletes an assignment, 204 on success or 404 if absent
api.assignments.delete_id.never_for: deleting one still referenced by a workflow's WorkflowAssignments row — the restrict FK raises SQLSTATE 23001, surfaced as 422
